//: homepage -- the PRODUCTION artifact, built with `./build_it_please.sh --profile homepage`.
This file replaced the `--homepage` flag, ten `if $homepage` branches in build_it_please.sh, an
`inHomepage` boolean on every part, and a per-flavour list of files to delete again at the end
of the build (arc 5). What production contains is now readable in three lines.
The parts are listed EXPLICITLY rather than as an exclusion, because this is a shipped artifact:
its contents should be visible in one place, and a part added to the partition tomorrow should
NOT silently join production. Today that list is the product plus the in-world inspectors --
meta-tools has always been in a production build, and a `lean` profile (arc 5 phase 2) is what
will drop it -- plus the example documents, which production has always shown and keeps showing:
'samples' is named here precisely so that splitting it out of core is a PACKAGING change and not
a visible one. The desktop's 'Examples' folder looks exactly as it did.
'maps' is named for the same reason but bought with a different mechanism: the sample dashboard
and the NYC slide BUILD maps, so production cannot simply drop that part. It is LAZY instead --
shipped, but not in js/pre-compiled.js and not fetched until a map is actually asked for. That is
the one shape that keeps the Examples whole while still taking the artwork off the first load.
'plots' and 'meta-tools' are lazy for the same reason: the samples build plots, and the
inspectors are the definition of on-demand -- nobody opens one during a normal session, and
opening one already had to await the reflective layer, so the part load joins an existing wait.
'spreadsheet' + 'spreadsheet-launcher' are ONE decision spelled as two parts, and both are named
here on purpose. The launcher is EAGER because WorldWdgt.createDesktop places its Examples-folder
icon at boot; the 114 KB grid behind it is LAZY, so production keeps the icon and stops carrying
the engine in js/pre-compiled.js. Naming one without the other is the mistake to avoid -- the
launcher alone is an icon whose click can only reject, the engine alone is code nothing opens.
Everything else about this tree FOLLOWS from these four facts, with nothing to maintain:
no harness part      -> no js/tests link, BUILDFLAG_LOAD_TESTS false, the tests-repo build
gates skipped, and the dead `if Automator?` branches stripped
index.html only      -> no SWCanvas boot bundle and no font-assets/ (~90 MB not deployed)
form precompiled     -> the pre-compile driver harvests the image from a compile-at-boot boot,
then it is minified in place; the world starts from that image
sources lazy         -> ...and the class source text is SHIPPED but not loaded until
something needs it: opening an inspector, or restoring a snapshot
that carries class-level source edits. That text is 2.28 MB, 62.7%
of this tree, so a visitor who never opens an inspector never
downloads it -- and the first one who does waits for it once.
`background` is the alternative (fetch it behind the running world,
the historical behaviour); `lean` is the profile that drops it
outright. Changing this line is the whole of that decision.
the absent parts      -> their assets and vendor payloads are simply never written (so no
fizzytiles 3D payload, no FileSaver/JSZip, no harness pointer icons)
